meta.title: Send Files From Android to iPhone — Free & Fast | BIShare
meta.description: Send files from Android to iPhone the easy way — photos, videos, and large files, device-to-device over Wi-Fi or a browser link. Free, no app on the iPhone.

hero.title: Send files from Android to iPhone
hero.body: Just switched phones, or need to hand a video to an iPhone friend? Android and iOS don’t share a nearby-transfer standard, so there’s no built-in way to do it. BIShare bridges them: push photos, videos, and files straight from your Android to any iPhone over the same Wi-Fi, or with a link the iPhone opens in Safari. Nothing to install on the iPhone.

why.title: Why Android and iPhone don’t talk to each other
why.body: Quick Share moves files quickly between Android phones and Windows, but it stops at the edge of Apple’s world — it simply can’t reach an iPhone. AirDrop is the mirror image: brilliant between Apple devices, blind to Android. So the everyday task of getting a clip off your Android and onto an iPhone falls straight through the gap. BIShare was built to close it — Android to iPhone, in both directions.

0.b: Pick the iPhone and send — files travel directly between the two phones, end-to-end encrypted, never parked on a server. It’s quick, and it still works from an Android hotspot when there’s no internet in sight.

1.h: When the iPhone is far away
1.b: BIShare hands you a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. On the iPhone, open the link in Safari and tap download — no App Store trip, no account. Every link erases itself after 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux in one app. Send Android → iPhone today, iPhone → Android tomorrow, or phone → laptop the same way — one tool, every direction.

comparison.title: Quick Share vs AirDrop vs BIShare for Android → iPhone

0.q: Can I AirDrop from Android to an iPhone?
0.a: Not with AirDrop — it’s Apple-only and can’t see an Android phone at all. BIShare does the same job across both: on shared Wi-Fi it sends directly, phone to phone; when you’re apart it gives you a link the iPhone opens in Safari to download the file.

1.q: How do I send a video from Android to iPhone without losing quality?
1.a: BIShare transfers the original file, so a 4K video arrives exactly as it left — none of the compression messaging apps add. Send it directly over Wi-Fi, or through a share link the iPhone downloads at full resolution.

2.q: Does the iPhone need to install anything?
2.a: No. For a share link, the iPhone just opens it in Safari or any browser and downloads — no app, no account on their side. Installing BIShare on both phones makes nearby transfers faster and unlocks every feature, but it’s never required to receive.

3.q: What’s the largest file I can send from Android to iPhone?
3.a: Over the same Wi-Fi there’s no size cap — the two phones talk directly, so whole photo libraries or long 4K clips are fine. Free share links carry files up to 100 GB, plenty for almost anything you’d hand off.

4.a: Yes — free, with no account and no ads. Nearby transfers over your own network are unlimited, and browser share links work for anyone, on any phone or computer.

cta.title: Get any file from your Android onto an iPhone in seconds
cta.body: Free, no account. Install BIShare on your Android and start sending — the iPhone doesn’t even need the app to receive.
